meta.association: Translated CAG repeat expansion in exon 1 of ATXN2 encoding an elongated polyglutamine tract in ataxin-2. The normal allele range is 14-30 repeats, 31-34 is intermediate, and 35-500 is pathogenic. Normal alleles carry CAA interruptions; pathogenic alleles are typically pure CAG.

evidence.reference_title: Moderate expansion of a normally biallelic trinucleotide repeat in spinocerebellar ataxia type 2.
evidence.snippet: In SCA2 patients, the repeat was perfect and expanded to 36-52 repeats. The most common disease allele contained (CAG)37, one of the shortest expansions seen in a CAG expansion syndrome.

nodes.description: Reducing ATXN2 expression addresses the initiating lesion rather than a downstream consequence. In two SCA2 mouse models the lead oligonucleotide ASO7 delayed phenotype onset and restored Purkinje cell firing frequency even when started more than 12 weeks after motor onset, which is the strongest available argument that the electrophysiological lesion is reversible. This is preclinical; no ASO is approved for SCA2.

evidence.reference_title: Antisense oligonucleotide therapy for spinocerebellar ataxia type 2.
evidence.snippet: Notably, the firing frequency of Purkinje cells returned to normal even when treatment was initiated more than 12 weeks after the onset of the motor phenotype in BAC-Q72 mice.

nodes.description: Expresses the full-length human ATXN2 gene under its own regulatory machinery, so expression is not restricted to one cell type. The wild-type-repeat BAC-Q22 line is the matched control and is indistinguishable from wild type, which is a genuine internal negative control for repeat length rather than for transgenesis.

PolyQ-expanded ataxin-2 misfolds and forms microaggregates. This is the node at which SCA2 departs from the polyglutamine stereotype set by Huntington disease and SCA3: in SCA2 brains the aggregates are cytoplasmic, not nuclear, and transgenic ataxin-2[Q58] remains cytoplasmic without detectable ubiquitination while still producing progressive Purkinje cell loss. Neither nuclear localization nor inclusion-body formation is necessary for pathogenesis. Curators extending this entry should not "correct" it toward the nuclear-inclusion pattern; the cytoplasmic localization is the experimentally supported claim and is what differentiates SCA2 within the Polyglutamine Disorders grouping.

evidence.reference_title: Nuclear localization or inclusion body formation of ataxin-2 are not necessary for SCA2 pathogenesis in mouse or human.
evidence.snippet: In SCA2 brains, we found cytoplasmic, but not nuclear, microaggregates.

evidence.reference_title: Nuclear localization or inclusion body formation of ataxin-2 are not necessary for SCA2 pathogenesis in mouse or human.
evidence.snippet: Mice expressing ataxin-2 with Q58 showed progressive functional deficits accompanied by loss of the Purkinje cell dendritic arbor and finally loss of Purkinje cells.

nodes.description: The initiating lesion is a CAG repeat in exon 1 of ATXN2 expanded beyond the pathogenic threshold of approximately 35 copies, within the translated reading frame, so the tract is expressed as an elongated polyglutamine domain in ataxin-2. Normal alleles are 14-30 copies and carry CAA interruptions; pathogenic alleles are typically pure CAG, and loss of the interruption is itself part of the lesion rather than an incidental detail. Repeat length is inversely correlated with age of onset.

genetic_context.description: Germline expansion of the exon 1 CAG tract beyond ~35 copies. The consequence is a toxic gain of function of the expanded protein, with a concurrent partial loss of ataxin-2's normal translational-regulatory function.

nodes.description: This node is deliberately kept off the main SCA2 chain. Intermediate-length ATXN2 polyglutamine expansions are an established risk factor for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, acting by modifying TDP-43 toxicity rather than through the cytoplasmic polyQ aggregation route that drives SCA2 itself. It is a susceptibility claim about a different disease, not a step in SCA2 pathogenesis, and is curated here because the same locus carries both. Reported length bands differ by source and are not reconciled: Elden et al. report 27-33 glutamines for ALS association, while STRchive's intermediate band is 31-34. Note the boundary is not absolute - FTLD-ALS with TDP-43 pathology has been described in a family carrying a full ataxin-2 expansion - so full-expansion carriers should not be described as categorically free of motor neuron disease.
nodes.id: Intermediate-Length ATXN2 Allele as an ALS Risk Modifier

evidence.reference_title: Ataxin-2 intermediate-length polyglutamine expansions are associated with increased risk for ALS.
evidence.snippet: We found that intermediate-length polyQ expansions (27-33 glutamines) in ATXN2 were significantly associated with ALS. These data establish ATXN2 as a relatively common ALS susceptibility gene.

evidence.reference_title: Therapeutic reduction of ataxin-2 extends lifespan and reduces pathology in TDP-43 mice.
evidence.snippet: The decrease in ataxin-2 reduced aggregation of TDP-43, markedly increased survival and improved motor function.

nodes.description: Normal ataxin-2 is an RNA-binding translational regulator: it interacts with the DEAD/H-box helicase DDX6 and with poly(A)-binding protein, and its concentration governs assembly of stress granules and P-bodies. PolyQ expansion impairs selective mRNA binding - shown directly for RGS8 mRNA, whose protein product attenuates mGluR1 signalling. This node is curated as a disease-specific translational lesion rather than as conformance to the module's "Transcriptional Dysregulation" node, because ataxin-2 is an RNA and translation regulator, not a transcription factor; asserting transcriptional conformance here would import a claim from the HD/SCA17 pattern that SCA2's own evidence does not make.

evidence.snippet: Using RNA immunoprecipitation we showed that ATXN2 interacted selectively with RGS8 mRNA. This interaction was impaired when ATXN2 harbored an expanded polyglutamine.

nodes.description: SCA2 produces early and severe degeneration of the olivopontocerebellar system - cerebellar cortex, pontine nuclei and inferior olives - extending with progression to substantia nigra, striatum, pallidum and eventually neocortex, while the dentate nucleus is consistently spared. This distribution is broader than the purely cerebellar SCAs and overlaps regions affected in Huntington disease, and it accounts for the parkinsonian and cognitive features that appear later in the course.

evidence.reference_title: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 2 (SCA2) - neuropathological findings in eleven Cuban patients.
evidence.snippet: The degeneration of the olivopontocerebellar regions as in classical olivopontocerebellar atrophy occurred early and severely in SCA2.

evidence.reference_title: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 2 (SCA2) - neuropathological findings in eleven Cuban patients.
evidence.snippet: The neuropathological progression soon included neuronal loss in the substantia nigra, striatum, pallidum and later even the neocortex, while the dentate nucleus was consistently spared.

nodes.description: A Purkinje-cell-targeted full-length ATXN2 transgenic that establishes the temporal ordering on which the therapeutic rationale depends: firing frequency falls before motor signs, and both precede cell loss.

Mutant ataxin-2 binds the cytosolic C-terminal region of the type 1 inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptor and increases its sensitivity to activation, producing exaggerated calcium release in Purkinje cells and increased vulnerability to glutamate. The pharmacological arm of this claim is unusually strong for a mechanism node: the ryanodine-receptor inhibitor and calcium stabilizer dantrolene both attenuates glutamate-induced death in culture and reduces Purkinje cell loss in the SCA2-58Q mouse.

nodes.description: Purkinje cells lose intrinsic firing frequency well before they are lost. In the ATXN2-Q127 mouse, firing frequency falls from 6 weeks and tracks motor deterioration, while Purkinje cell number is preserved until after 12 weeks. This ordering is the mechanistic rationale for ATXN2-lowering therapy: the treatable lesion is an electrophysiological one that precedes irreversible cell loss, and ASO treatment restores firing even when started after motor onset.

evidence.snippet: Although motor performance began to deteriorate at 8 weeks of age, reductions in PC number were not seen until after 12 weeks. Decreases in the PC firing frequency first showed at 6 weeks and paralleled deterioration of motor performance with progression of disease.

nodes.description: Age of onset is inversely correlated with repeat length, and intergenerational instability produces anticipation. Progression is not linear: in a prospective cohort, SARA scores advanced 0.35 points per year before 10 years of disease duration and 2.45 points per year after it, which matters directly for trial design because disease duration, not baseline severity, sets the expected rate.

evidence.snippet: Then an acceleration was detected after 10 years of disease duration: SARA scores progressed 0.35 before and 2.45 points/year after this deadline (p = 0.013).

evidence.snippet: Age at onset, mutation severity, and presence of amyotrophy, parkinsonism, dystonic manifestations and cognitive decline at baseline did not influence the rate of disease progression.
